explanation: Q1 selects flights with the maximum actual_time per origin, using a subquery to find the max per origin and joining back. Q2 uses a self-join to compute the max actual_time per origin for each (origin, dest, actual_time) group. The difference arises when multiple destinations share the same max actual_time for the same origin, but Q1's DISTINCT may collapse rows differently than Q2's grouping logic.
counterexample_dsp: Create two origins (A and B) with flights having max actual_time 200. Add a flight from origin A to a new destination with actual_time 200. Q1 will include all such flights, while Q2 may return only one due to grouping.
